questions.prompt: Which of the following is primarily a board (governance) responsibility rather than a management responsibility?

options.text: Scheduling program volunteers for the spring event
Approving the annual budget and strategic plan
Choosing which software the office uses for email
Hiring the program coordinator

questions.explanation: The board sets direction and approves the budget and strategic plan. Day-to-day decisions, including hiring staff other than the ED/CEO, belong to management.

questions.prompt: Your board opens each meeting with a land acknowledgement read from a script. A new director asks what the organization actually does to support reconciliation. What is the most helpful response?

options.text: The acknowledgement is enough. It shows respect, and anything more is management’s job
Treat the question as a governance matter: ask what relationships, commitments and actions sit behind the acknowledgement, and consider making it part of strategy and board learning
Stop doing land acknowledgements to avoid seeming insincere
Ask the one Indigenous director to decide what the board should do

questions.explanation: Reconciliation is part of the board’s strategy, accountability and culture. A meaningful acknowledgement is specific and connected to action, and the whole board shares responsibility for learning and relationships.

questions.prompt: A director was nominated to the board by a major funder. When a decision is in the organization’s best interest but not the funder’s, the director should:

options.text: Vote as the funder would want, since that is why they were appointed
Act in the best interests of the organization, and treat the divergence as a potential conflict to declare
Ask the funder for written instructions before voting
Resign immediately

questions.explanation: A director’s duty of loyalty is owed to the organization, regardless of who nominated them. Divergent interests should be declared and managed as a conflict.

questions.prompt: Which best describes how directors meet the duty of care?

options.text: By ensuring every decision produces a good result
By having professional qualifications in finance or law
By deferring to the Chair on difficult matters
By preparing, attending, asking questions and exercising reasonable judgment

questions.explanation: The duty of care is about a diligent, informed process. Courts generally protect informed, good-faith decisions even when outcomes are poor.

questions.prompt: The board is reviewing bids for a contract. One bidder is owned by a director’s brother. What should the director do?

options.text: Declare the interest, abstain from the vote and leave the meeting for the discussion
Stay and vote, but mention the relationship if anyone asks
Stay for the discussion but abstain from voting
Nothing, as long as the brother’s bid is the lowest

questions.explanation: Declare, Abstain, Leave. The declaration and the abstention should be recorded in the minutes.

questions.prompt: After a vigorous debate, the board approves a decision you voted against. A local reporter asks for your view. You should:

options.text: Explain that you disagreed and why
Say “no comment” and post your concerns on social media instead
Support the board’s decision publicly, or refer the reporter to the board’s designated spokesperson
Share the confidential board discussion so the public can judge

questions.explanation: The board speaks with one voice. You can ask for your dissent to be recorded in the minutes, but you should not undermine a board decision in public.

questions.prompt: Which financial statement shows whether the organization has enough cash coming in to pay its bills as they come due?

options.text: Statement of operations
Statement of cash flows
The strategic plan
The annual return filed with the corporate registry

questions.explanation: The statement of cash flows shows where cash came from and went. An organization can report a surplus and still run short of cash.

questions.prompt: Cash is tight, and the ED/CEO proposes temporarily using a foundation grant restricted to a youth program to cover general payroll. What is the main concern?

options.text: There is no concern if the money is repaid within the fiscal year
Payroll is a management issue the board should not discuss
It would affect the organization’s disbursement quota
Restricted funds must be used for their stated purpose. Diverting them can breach the grant agreement and damage trust.

questions.explanation: Restricted funds carry obligations to the donor or funder. The board should look at other solutions, such as reserves, a line of credit or a conversation with the funder.

questions.prompt: Directors in Canada can be personally liable if the organization fails to:

options.text: Remit employee source deductions (income tax, CPP, EI) to the CRA
Meet its fundraising targets
Hold a board retreat each year
Achieve the goals in its strategic plan

questions.explanation: Unremitted source deductions (and collected GST/HST) can create personal liability for directors. Ask for confirmation at every meeting that remittances are current.

questions.prompt: Which statement about nonprofits and registered charities is correct?

options.text: All nonprofits can issue official donation receipts
A registered charity may endorse a political candidate who supports its cause
Registered charity is a status granted by the CRA. Not every nonprofit is a registered charity.
Registered charities file their annual return only when the CRA requests it

questions.explanation: Only registered charities and other qualified donees can issue official receipts. Charities cannot engage in partisan activity, and they must file the T3010 every year.

questions.prompt: A registered charity must file its T3010 information return:

options.text: Within six months of its fiscal year-end
Within 30 days of its annual general meeting
Every three years
Only if it received government funding

questions.explanation: The T3010 is due within six months of fiscal year-end everywhere in Canada, and late filing can lead to revocation. Provincial and federal corporate filings, such as annual returns, have their own separate deadlines.

questions.prompt: A staff member approaches you privately to complain about the ED/CEO’s decisions. The best response is to:

options.text: Promise to raise it at the next board meeting and keep the staff member’s name confidential
Listen respectfully, avoid taking sides or giving direction, point them to the proper channel, and inform the Chair
Investigate the complaint yourself by interviewing other staff
Instruct the ED/CEO to reverse the decisions

questions.explanation: Individual directors should not go around the ED/CEO. Concerns should move through proper channels, such as HR or whistleblower policies, with the Chair informed.

questions.prompt: Which is a core board responsibility regarding the Executive Director/CEO?

options.text: Approving each staff hire the ED/CEO makes
Reviewing the ED/CEO’s emails to ensure quality
Supervising the ED/CEO’s daily schedule
Conducting a fair, documented annual performance evaluation against agreed goals

questions.explanation: The board hires, sets goals for, evaluates, compensates and plans succession for the ED/CEO, and leaves day-to-day management to them.

questions.prompt: Between meetings, the Chair and Treasurer agree by phone to approve a large unbudgeted expense beyond the ED/CEO’s authority. Unless authority has been formally delegated to them:

options.text: The expense is approved because the two most senior officers agreed
The expense is approved if it is recorded in the next minutes
The board has not approved it. It needs a proper board meeting or a written resolution under the bylaws.
The ED/CEO can approve it if the Chair agrees

questions.explanation: Authority rests with the board acting together through proper process. Individual directors, even officers, cannot bind the board unless authority has been formally delegated.

questions.prompt: What is the board’s role in risk management?

options.text: To eliminate all risk to the organization
To decide how much risk is acceptable and ensure major risks are identified, monitored and managed
To leave risk entirely to the auditor
To discuss risk only after something goes wrong

questions.explanation: Boards oversee risk. They set risk tolerance, review a risk register regularly and confirm that safeguards such as D&O insurance are in place.
